name: EWF Universal Championship
epitaph: Elite Wrestling Foundation put its own top belt up as a tournament before it had a champion at all. The first round ran on the fed’s first Immortality, 9 March 2003, and the final closed WrestleFest: Turbulence beat “The Turnbuckle” Jay to be handed the belt and, in the fed’s own commentator’s words, to become “the very first EWF Champion”. He was still carrying it at the last capture of the champions page, six weeks later, and the fed left nothing dated after that.
notes: The fed’s own rules page describes a quite different set of belts — a World Title, an Intercontinental Title, an EWF Title and World Tag Team Titles — which its champions page never uses. Both are held; the rules read as a template the fed never brought into line with what it crowned.

name: EWF International Championship
epitaph: The International Championship was decided at WrestleFest 2003, where The Overweighter left with the belt. By the time the fed’s champions page was last captured, six weeks later, it had passed to Super Rob; nothing the fed left records how.

name: EWF International Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Blood Man and J won this belt vacant at WrestleFest 2003, eliminating John Dumas and Chaos in a tag team elimination match — Blood Man pinned Dumas behind the referee’s back with a chair, then the pair finished Chaos with Blood Man’s Bleeding Blood and J’s own J Splash. They were still champions, by the fed’s own commentary and ring announcement called simply the “Tag team championship,” when Jay Krazy, Dumas and Chaos jumped them celebrating the win, and were still holding it six weeks later at the champions page’s last capture, there billed the “International Tag Team” champions. No other holder appears anywhere in what the Elite Wrestling Foundation left.
